question.worked_solution:
We can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{4}{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{4/5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{4/5+1}}{(\frac{4}{5}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{9/5}}{(\frac{9}{5})}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{9/5}}{9}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{9/5}}{9}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{9/5}}{9})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{5}{9}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{9/5})+0 & = \\ \frac{5}{9}\cdot \frac{9}{5}{x}^{9/5-1} & = \\ {x}^{4/5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
